units.sentence: In districts without limits, phones can stay in class, which the new law treats as a di...

What the law prohibits 'to minimize distractions' (P-057) is student access (P-007), not phones being in the room. As worded, the sentence credits the law with a view it doesn't hold.
units.suggested_fix: 'In districts without limits, students can use phones in class; the new law bans that access "to minimize distractions."'

By standard convention a continued quote belongs to the same speaker, so the attribution holds. The quoted words are verbatim, and 'the ban' paraphrases 'distraction-free legislation'.

units.sentence: So the statewide K-8 rule hadn't yet taken effect when the high school ban was signed.
units.problem: The conclusion doesn't follow from 'the two dates'. July 1, 2026 is a 'no later than' start date (P-006), so schools could start earlier. The K-8 law was already in force (HB 340, signed in 2025, P-028), and its policy deadline of January 1, 2026 (P-020) had passed. What follows is only that the K-8 ban wasn't yet required everywhere. 'Taken effect' also clashes with the page's own usage, which keeps the effective date (Dec 31, 2026) separate from the compliance deadline.
units.suggested_fix: 'So schools weren't yet required to enforce the K-8 rule statewide when the high school ban was signed.'
